1. Core Clinical Tension: A 34-year-old postpartum woman presents with sciatic-like radicular low back pain and mild right iliac fossa tenderness without fever or spinal deformity. The initial clinical impression of lumbar radiculopathy/sciatica is shattered when imaging reveals a massive 720-mL psoas abscess. The primary diagnostic dilemma is distinguishing a pyogenic retroperitoneal abscess or postpartum pelvic infection from a cold primary tuberculous psoas abscess, especially in the absence of skeletal vertebral involvement (Pott's disease) and with initial negative pus AFB smears, PCR, and cultures.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Concludes immediately following the initial lumbar and abdominal CT scan demonstrating the large 720-mL psoas collection with normal adjacent bony structures, strictly prior to percutaneous aspiration, empirical intravenous antibiotic therapy, repeat surgical exploration, and abscess wall histopathology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Sciatic radiculopathy is excluded by abdominal/lumbar CT demonstrating a massive fluid collection displacing retroperitoneal tissues. Acute pyogenic bacterial psoas abscess (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus or polymicrobial pelvic source) is excluded by normal procalcitonin (0.316 ng/mL), afebrile state, negative routine bacterial cultures, and failure of broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy with rapid fluid re-accumulation. Primary tuberculous psoas abscess is confirmed by open biopsy of the thick fibrotic abscess wall demonstrating epithelioid giant cells and caseous necrosis.
case_prompt:
A 34-year-old biparous woman presents two months postpartum following an uneventful full-term pregnancy and spontaneous vaginal delivery with severe, debilitating right-sided low back pain radiating down the posterior right lower extremity in a sciatic distribution. She has no significant past medical history. Her symptoms were initially managed symptomatically as postpartum sciatic neuropathy at an outside clinic without sustained relief.

On physical examination, she is afebrile with normal vital signs. Palpation of the abdomen reveals localized mild deep tenderness in the right iliac fossa without peritoneal signs or palpable organomegaly. Neurological examination of the lower extremities shows intact motor strength, symmetric deep tendon reflexes, and no focal sensory deficits. Obstetric and gynecologic examinations are entirely normal, and cardiopulmonary examination is unremarkable.

Initial laboratory investigations reveal a normal leukocyte count of 7,300/mm³, hemoglobin of 10.9 g/dL, a markedly elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 102 mg/L, and a normal procalcitonin level of 0.316 ng/mL. Retroviral serology for HIV-1 and HIV-2 is non-reactive. Computed tomography (CT) imaging of the lumbar spine and abdomen demonstrates an unexpectedly large, well-encapsulated fluid collection in the right psoas muscle measuring 18 × 10 × 8 cm (approximate volume of 720 mL), without cortical erosions, disc space narrowing, or inflammatory changes involving the lumbar spine, intervertebral discs, or right sacroiliac joint.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Postpartum sciatic neuropathy / Lumbar disc herniation
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although presenting with classic radiating low back pain that led to initial symptomatic treatment, CT imaging showed normal intervertebral discs and identified a massive 720-mL retroperitoneal fluid collection as the true compressive etiology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The symptoms were initially misdiagnosed as a sciatic neuropathy and she was treated symptomatically at another medical center with a good outcome... Spinal lumbar and abdominal computed tomography scans (CT-scan) surprisingly showed a large right psoas abscess measuring 18 x 10 x 8 cm (a volume of about 720 mL).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pyogenic bacterial psoas abscess (Staphylococcus aureus / Enteric polymicrobial)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A typical acute pyogenic etiology was ruled out by the afebrile presentation, normal procalcitonin level, persistently sterile purulent aspirate on multiple standard bacterial and fungal cultures, and rapid recurrence of the abscess despite parenteral broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Culture failed to grow any microorganisms (including mycobacterium and mycoses). She was treated with gentamicin, amoxicillin/clavulanate, and metronidazole parenterally... However, a repeat CT-scan of the abdomen and the pelvis showed a re-accumulation of the right psoas collection measuring approximately 400 mL.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Primary Tuberculous Psoas Abscess
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Despite initial negative aspirate AFB stain, PCR, and cultures, open surgical drainage with full-thickness biopsy of the fibrotic abscess wall demonstrated characteristic epithelioid giant cells and caseous necrosis, establishing primary tuberculous psoas abscess without osseous spinal involvement.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: However, a diagnosis of tuberculosis was established after identification of epitheloid giant cells and caseous necrosis on the fibrotic abscess wall biopsy.

editor_comments: Classic demonstration of an isolated primary cold tuberculous psoas abscess presenting in the postpartum period, without underlying Pott's disease. Clean admission breakpoint.
